key_terms.meaning: A combinational block that adds three input bits a, b, cᵢₙ and gives sum s = a ⊕ b ⊕ cᵢₙ and carry cₒᵤₜ = ab + bcᵢₙ + acᵢₙ.
g = a·b (this bit makes a carry) and p = a ⊕ b (this bit passes an incoming carry on).
N full adders chained so each carry enters the next stage; the delay grows linearly with N.
Adder that computes carries directly from g and p with two-level AND-OR logic instead of waiting for them to ripple.
G = g₃ + p₃g₂ + p₃p₂g₁ + p₃p₂p₁g₀ and P = p₃p₂p₁p₀, which let a 4-bit block be treated as one big bit.
Two copies of a block compute with carry-in 0 and 1; a multiplexer picks the right sum when the real carry arrives.
A row of full adders that adds three numbers and produces sum and carry vectors without resolving carries, so the carry is delayed, not rippled.
A block whose propagate chain ORs to a single bypass signal; if the block only propagates, the carry jumps over it through one AND-OR path.
One row of the multiplication table, formed as aᵢ · B, that is shifted left by i bit positions before adding.
Array multiplier for unsigned numbers: one AND gate per partial product bit and a square array of adders with a fixed, regular layout.
Two's complement array multiplier that keeps the regular array shape and fixes sign by inverting some partial product bits and adding two correction constants.
Adder tree that reduces many partial product rows to two using layers of 3:2 counters, so delay grows as log of the number of rows.
A full adder used as a counter: it takes three bits of equal weight and outputs two bits of weights 2 and 1, reducing the row count by one.
Rewriting the multiplier in radix-4 signed digits from bit pairs, so a run of 1s becomes few non-zero digits and the number of partial products halves.
A circuit with n inputs and 2ⁿ outputs where exactly one output is active for each input code; the minterm generator of combinational logic.
A circuit that passes one of 2ⁿ data inputs to a single output under the control of n select bits.
A circuit that compares two n-bit words and asserts equal, greater-than or less-than using cascaded equality and magnitude signals.
A storage element that copies D to Q while the clock is high and holds the last value while the clock is low.
Data must be stable for tₛᵤ before the clock edge and tₕ after it; violating either can make the register store a wrong or metastable value.
Two cross-coupled CMOS inverters plus two access transistors; it holds a bit as long as power is on and needs no refresh.
One access transistor and one capacitor storing charge; the bit leaks away and must be refreshed every few milliseconds.
A cross-coupled latch that detects the small voltage difference the cell places on the bitline pair and drives it to a full logic level.

takeaways: A wide adder is a carry problem, not an addition problem: every adder family is a different answer to how soon the last stage learns its carry.
A carry look-ahead adder turns the ripple into a tree of generate and propagate terms, trading silicon area and heavy fan-in for logarithmic delay.
Carry select, carry skip and carry save each dodge the carry chain in a different way: predict both answers, bypass a propagating block, or postpone the carry.
An array multiplier is regular and easy to lay out, but its delay includes one long diagonal carry ripple from the top-right to the bottom-left corner.
The Wallace tree removes that ripple by summing columns as a tree of 3:2 counters, cutting the delay to roughly log of the number of partial products.
Booth recoding attacks the number of rows instead of the number of adders, halving the partial products for radix-4 and handling signed numbers naturally.
Decoders, multiplexers and comparators are the glue of a datapath: a decoder makes minterms, a multiplexer selects a result, and a comparator makes the branch decision.
A latch is level-sensitive and a register is edge-triggered; two latches in series with opposite clocks give you the edge that makes synchronous design predictable.
An SRAM bit is a feedback loop kept alive by power, while a DRAM bit is charge on a capacitor that leaks away and must be refreshed.
Memory speed comes from parallelism: the row decoder activates a whole word at once, and the sense amplifiers decide many bits at the same time.
bank_note: Long answers are marked on the circuit or block diagram, the delay expression in terms of full-adder or gate delays, and a clear area-versus-speed verdict, so sketch first and then justify the numbers.

bank.q: Draw the transistor-level CMOS full adder and write its sum and carry functions. Build a 4-bit ripple carry adder from it and explain why its delay grows with the word length.
outline: Sum = a ⊕ b ⊕ cᵢₙ, carry = ab + cᵢₙ(a ⊕ b)
Carry is generated in two gate delays, sum in three
4-bit chain: cₒᵤₜ of each stage is the cᵢₙ of the next
Worst-case delay = N × carry delay of one stage
Area grows linearly, wiring is simple and regular

bank.q: Define carry generate and carry propagate for one bit. Derive the carry expressions c₁ to c₄ for a 4-bit carry look-ahead adder and explain what limits block size.
outline: gᵢ = aᵢbᵢ, pᵢ = aᵢ ⊕ bᵢ
cᵢ₊₁ = gᵢ + pᵢcᵢ expanded for each stage
Two-level AND-OR realisation gives constant delay per block
Fan-in and gate count grow fast with block width
Group generate and group propagate used to cascade 4-bit blocks

bank.q: Explain with block diagrams how a carry select adder, a carry save adder and a carry skip adder each reduce the effect of the carry chain.
outline: Carry select: duplicate blocks for cᵢₙ = 0 and 1, multiplexer selects
Multiplexer delay replaces the ripple through the block
Carry save: three operands to two vectors, carry postponed to a final CPA
Carry skip: block propagate OR drives a bypass multiplexer
Comparison of area overhead and delay gain

bank.q: Describe the 6T SRAM cell and the 1T1C DRAM cell. Compare them on area per bit, speed, retention and refresh requirement.
outline: 6T: two cross-coupled inverters plus two access transistors
Read and write through complementary bitlines, no refresh
1T1C: one transistor plus a capacitor, charge stored on the capacitor
Leakage forces periodic refresh
DRAM is denser and cheaper per bit, SRAM is faster and simpler to use

bank.q: Explain the D latch and the master-slave D flip-flop with a timing diagram. Define setup time, hold time and clock-to-Q delay.
outline: Latch is transparent when clock is high, holds when low
Two latches with opposite clocks give edge triggering
Master captures on one edge, slave delivers on the next
Setup and hold windows around the active edge
Clock-to-Q is the delay from edge to valid output

bank.q: Draw the partial product array of a 4×4 Braun multiplier. Show where each full adder and half adder sits and estimate the worst-case delay in full-adder delays.
outline: AND gates form aᵢbⱼ at fixed array positions
Rows added from the top with carry flowing down the diagonal
Half adders at the array edges, full adders inside
Worst-case path is the diagonal from the top-right to the bottom-left
Delay quoted as a multiple of the full-adder carry delay

bank.q: Using Baugh-Wooley, multiply the 4-bit two's complement numbers 1011 and 0110. Show the inverted partial product bits and the correction constants added in the array.
outline: Identify sign bits a₃ and b₃
Invert the sign-related partial product bits
Add the two correction terms in the appropriate columns
Complete the array addition and read the 8-bit product
Explain why the array shape stays regular

bank.q: A 16-bit adder is built from four 4-bit blocks. Apply carry skip to the blocks and derive the worst-case carry delay in terms of block carry delay and multiplexer delay. Compare with the plain ripple delay.
outline: Block propagate P = p₃p₂p₁p₀
Bypass path through one AND-OR multiplexer per block
Worst case = block carry delay + number of skipped blocks × multiplexer delay + last block carry delay
Compare against 16 × one-bit carry delay
Note that alternating skip and ripple blocks improves the constant

bank.q: Design a 3-to-8 decoder with an active-high enable using NAND gates. Use it and a few gates to realise f = Σm(1, 3, 5, 7) and state the gate count.
outline: Three inverters generate the complemented inputs
Eight NAND gates, one per minterm, gated by the enable
Active-low outputs if NAND outputs are used directly
OR the selected minterms with a NAND-NAND or OR gate
Function reduces to f = c, a useful check

bank.q: Build an 8:1 multiplexer from 2:1 multiplexers and show how the same structure stored in a register implements a 4-input lookup table for an FPGA logic cell.
outline: Tree of 2:1 stages, three select levels for eight inputs
Select lines split into most and least significant groups
Seven 2:1 multiplexers for an 8:1
Lookup table stores the truth table in flip-flops feeding the multiplexer tree
Any four-variable function is realised by loading sixteen bits

bank.q: Compare ripple carry, carry look-ahead, carry select and carry skip adders for an N-bit word on area, delay and wiring complexity. Which would you choose at N = 64 and why?
outline: Delay order: ripple linear, look-ahead and skip logarithmic, select linear but with a smaller constant
Area order: ripple smallest, carry select largest for small blocks
Wiring and layout regularity favour ripple and select
Mixed schemes such as block look-ahead inside skip blocks
Justified choice with the trade-off stated explicitly

bank.q: Compare an array multiplier with a Wallace tree multiplier for 16×16 bits on delay, area and layout regularity. Explain how Booth recoding changes the picture.
outline: Array delay dominated by the diagonal carry ripple, area regular and compact
Wallace tree delay grows as log of rows but wires are irregular and long
Counter count and interconnect congestion in the tree
Booth radix-4 halves the partial products, reducing both tree depth and array height
Recommendation depends on whether regularity or speed dominates the design

bank.q: Analyse the timing of a master-slave register in a pipeline: clock-to-Q, setup time, hold time and the minimum clock period. Explain how clock skew can cause a hold violation.
outline: Path from launch edge to capture edge fixes the clock period
tperiod ≥ tclock-to-Q + tlogic + tsetup + skew
Hold check uses the same edge and the short path
Skew subtracts from the hold margin
Two-phase non-overlapping clocks avoid transparency races

bank.q: A system needs 1 Mbit of on-chip storage and 1 Gbit of main memory. Evaluate the choice of 6T SRAM for the first and 1T1C DRAM for the second, covering cell size, speed, refresh, sense amplifier design and standby power.
outline: SRAM cell is about six transistors, DRAM cell about one transistor and one capacitor
SRAM read is differential and fast, DRAM needs charge sensing and restore
DRAM refresh consumes bandwidth and standby power
Sense amplifiers and precharge needed in both, but DRAM timing is tighter
Conclusion: SRAM for speed-critical caches, DRAM for density

glossary.def: A two-input circuit producing a sum bit a ⊕ b and a carry bit ab.
Passing the carry out of one adder stage into the next, so carries travel through the whole word.
Computing carries in parallel from generate and propagate signals instead of waiting for them to ripple.
A carry computed for a group of bits using that group's generate and propagate terms.
A dynamic chain of pass transistors that propagates or kills a carry along a block.
An adder that precomputes sums for both possible carry inputs and selects one with a multiplexer.
A structured full-adder array that reduces three numbers to two without resolving carries.
An adder block that bypasses the carry straight to the next block when every bit only propagates.
The shifted multiplicand row produced by one multiplier bit before the rows are summed.
A multiplier built as a regular two-dimensional array of AND gates and adders.
A two's complement array multiplication scheme using bit inversion and correction constants to keep the array regular.
A tree of 3:2 counters that reduces partial product rows to two in logarithmic depth.
A multiplier that uses the minimum number of counters at each stage, at the cost of irregular wiring.
Recoding the multiplier bits into signed digits so that fewer partial products are needed.
A circuit that asserts exactly one of 2ⁿ outputs for each n-bit input code.
A selector that connects one of several inputs to a single output under select control.
A circuit that reports whether two binary words are equal, or which one is larger.
A level-sensitive storage element that is transparent for half the clock period.
An edge-triggered storage element that samples data only at a clock transition.
The unresolved state a storage element may enter when its input changes inside the setup-hold window.
The row wire a decoder drives to connect a whole row of memory cells to their bitlines.
The column wire that carries the stored bit from the selected cell to the sense amplifier.
A small cross-coupled amplifier that resolves the weak bitline signal into a full logic level.
Periodic rewriting of DRAM cells to replace charge lost by leakage.
